Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then use the wake-visual-signals skill to inspect the required rollout keyframes before touching the target policy. I’ll keep the work confined to this Phase 2 workspace and produce exactly one candidate plus both required documentation updates.

The visual-first skill applies because the sampled examples include wake keyframe sheets. I’m using it to anchor any controller change in the release-to-termination motion, then cross-check that reading against trajectory, flow, force, and stability metrics.

The shared prewarm shows the fixed fish beginning above and downstream of a fully developed four-street wake; the successful release sheet shows a large looping approach before final capture, so there is room to improve arrival efficiency without sacrificing the corridor-acquisition mechanism. I’m now checking whether that loop is supported by the sampled time-series and whether any inherited failed trial isolates a safer feedback change.

The evidence supports a bounded corridor-retention probe. I’ll preserve the evaluated `20.25°/0.67` propulsion bundle and the proven `0.30` steering response whenever the fish is stalled or receding. Only during sustained positive closing will the rolling-window signal soften the effective bearing scale toward `0.32`, the symmetric counterpart to the harmful `0.28` sharpening. The closing-speed normalization (`0.05 L/time`) comes from the successful rollout’s average distance closure, and the hypothesis is now being recorded before the policy edit as required by the skill.

The single candidate, its provenance notes, and the durable experience update are now in place. The guidance revision promotes the replicated `20.25°` result as evidence, adds the controlled `0.28` sharpening negative, and clearly labels the new closing-conditioned relief as an unevaluated test. I’m invoking the configured non-CFD checks now, separately as required.

The first configured check found the same rendered-metadata defect seen in the inherited logs: `README.md` marks the identical assigned parent twice, so the checker cannot resolve one parent. I’m removing only the duplicate marker entry, leaving the assigned parent and task contract unchanged, then rerunning the check.

The guidance check passes. The literal Julia command is not on `PATH` in this shell (the surrounding login profile also masks its exit status), so I’m following the inherited evaluation evidence to resolve the evaluator’s explicit Julia binary and will rerun the same lightweight assertion there. No CFD is being launched.

All three configured checks now pass: semantic guidance/provenance, the Julia policy contract via the evaluator’s explicit runtime, and the solver edit boundary. I’m doing a final audit of the closing gate, parameter schema, file deltas, and single-candidate constraint; this remains lightweight validation only.

Produced exactly one multi-wake candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1): preserves the proven gait and softly shifts bearing scale from `0.30` toward `0.32` only during positive rolling-window closure.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1): records the visual diagnosis, evidence, hypothesis, and falsification boundaries.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:36): materially updates the amplitude-threshold lesson and adds the negative `0.28` bearing-scale result.

The visual-first review specifically motivated closing-conditioned corridor retention instead of more amplitude or globally sharper steering. Guidance, Julia contract/schema, closing-gate, and boundary checks pass. No CFD was run.
